title: Back up and restore {name}: one file with all your work
description: A backup is one file with every task and file you keep in {name}. Make one from Settings › Your data, and restore it on any device.
answer: A backup is one file with all your tasks and files. Make one from {settings} › {data} with {download}, keep it where only you open it, and restore it on any device from the same place. Your keys are never in it.
tour.here: This is {settings} › {data}: everything {name} keeps here, and the copies you keep. Next time, {settings} is in your menu at the foot of the task list.
steps: Open {settings}, from your menu at the foot of the task list, then {data}.
Press {download}. Your browser saves one file, named Backup and today’s date.
Keep that file where only you open it: a USB key, or a folder of your own. Anyone who has it can read it.
To restore it, on this device or another: open {settings} › {data}, then {backup}.
Under {restore}, press {pick} and choose the file. What it holds is added to what is here; nothing here is deleted.
good: Your keys are never in a backup: after restoring on another device, put them in again in {brains}.
{data} says when the last backup was made, and says so too when a week has gone by and you have done more since.
A private window keeps nothing once it is closed, and clearing this site’s data in your browser deletes everything here. A backup is the way to keep it.
After your third task, {name} offers to make the first backup.
To bring in your history from ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini, it’s {import}, on the same page.
fixes: {name} says the file isn’t a backup
Choose the file {name} saved, named Backup and its date. An export from ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini goes through {import}.
Your browser keeps downloads in its own folder, often Downloads; on a phone, in Files. Its list of downloads shows where.
ask: When did I last back up, and how do I restore it on another computer?
